subject: Urban Planning
title: Fresh Kills: The World's Largest Landfill
description: A fast breakdown of Fresh Kills: The World's Largest Landfill for builders.

hook.text: Fresh Kills on Staten Island was the world's largest landfill — visible from space and taller than the Statue of Liberty.

buildup.text: For 53 years, New York dumped 150 million tons of garbage there. At its peak, 29,000 tons arrived daily by barge.

discovery.text: The landfill leaked toxins into groundwater and produced methane. Neighboring communities had elevated cancer rates.

twist.text: Fresh Kills closed in 2001 — then briefly reopened to receive debris from the World Trade Center collapse on September 11.

climax.text: Today, Fresh Kills is being transformed into a park three times the size of Central Park. Garbage became green space.

punchline.text: The world's biggest dump is becoming the city's newest park. Redemption takes time.

quiz.question: What is happening to Fresh Kills landfill today?
options: It's being mined for recyclable materials buried decades ago
It's being converted into a park three times the size of Central Park
It's been sealed and turned into a solar energy farm
